method_changes.note: Road network rebuilt: a node at least every 400 m, highway dead ends linked to the adjoining road, and no link across a county line or coastal water. This corrected in-town trips that had been routed the long way round (for example parts of Tucson, Kalispell, Spokane, Pueblo and Duluth). Sites in ZIP codes that span counties are now assigned to the county where most of the ZIP's residents live, and sites in ZIP codes larger than 100 square miles are placed at their city rather than at the centroid of the ZIP (which was 15 miles outside Billings and Great Falls). NCI centers are located at their hospital's ZIP code rather than the city center, and St. Jude Children's Research Hospital, which treats children, is no longer a distance target. On the same registry data (Sep 30, 2026) the national figures moved as follows: fewer than 20 trials within 60 miles 12.7% to 11.8%; none within 60 miles 4.4% to 3.8%; beyond 60 miles of a broad menu 38.8% to 38.1%; beyond 60 miles of an NCI center 44.2% to 43.7%; median distance to an NCI center 50 to 48 miles.

Which registry rows count as a place, and which studies count as cancer trials. A row that names a telemedicine or virtual service instead of a clinic is no longer a site: one fully decentralized study listed such a row in 107 cities, and it had been the only trial within 60 road-miles for about 346,000 residents 55+. Rows whose ZIP code is a typing error (the same named hospital is listed repeatedly in the stated city and never near that ZIP) are located where the registry's other rows list that hospital. The registry search now also asks by name for cancers it files outside its neoplasm category or has not coded (myelodysplastic syndromes, myelofibrosis, adenocarcinomas, glioblastoma, metastases: 107 more trials on Oct 5, 2026), and studies kept only for wording such as 'tumor necrosis factor' or 'non-malignant' are dropped (8 studies). On the same registry data (Sep 30, 2026) the telemedicine, ZIP and screening rules moved the national figures as follows: none within 60 miles 3.8% to 4.2%; fewer than 20 trials within 60 miles 11.8% to 12.0%; counties with any trial 848 to 833; distances to broad menus and NCI centers did not move. The wider search then added trials without moving these shares.

Where a registry row is counted and drawn. A row whose ZIP code has no Census area (a PO box or a hospital's own ZIP) took the county of the ZIP's first three digits even when its own city lay in another county, and was drawn at that county's center: 58 rows sat 43 to 251 miles from their city (31 Tawas City, Michigan rows in Tuscola County; Liberal, Kansas in Morton County; Pueblo in Conejos County, Colorado; Omaha in Lincoln County, Nebraska; Dallas in Cass County, Texas). The row's own city now decides the county and the row is drawn there; one spelling rule for city names (Saint/St., Fort/Ft., Lexington-Fayette, Nashville-Davidson) puts 21 more rows at their city. A trial for spread from a named cancer (to the brain, liver or peritoneum) is classified with that cancer (6 trials), and leptomeningeal disease counts as cancer (NCT07814352, which was in the Oct 5 pull but appears among the trials newly listed between Oct 5 and Oct 9). First used for the registry data of Oct 9, 2026 (pulled Oct 11). On the same registry data (Oct 5, 2026) these rules moved 194 site rows of 100 trials to another county and changed the trial count of 69 counties (Tuscola, Michigan 31 to 2; Iosco 0 to 31; Midland 1 to 12; Washtenaw 233 to 240; Stanly, North Carolina 2 to 9; Union, New Jersey 29 to 36; Pueblo, Colorado and Hudson, New Jersey 19 to 20); counties with any trial 838 to 833; none within 60 road-miles 4.2% to 4.3% (76,538 more residents 55+: 92 census tracts around Texarkana, North Platte, the San Luis Valley, northeast Alabama and the Oklahoma Panhandle lost a trial that existed only at a misplaced point, and 17 tracts gained one); fewer than 20 trials within 60 road-miles 12.0%, unchanged; distances to broad menus and NCI centers did not move. The registry's own changes between Oct 5 and Oct 9 moved no one across 'none within 60 road-miles' and added 57,428 residents 55+ to 'fewer than 20' (still 12.0%).

Where a site is drawn, which rows are cancer trials, and how trials are classified by cancer type; first applied at the refresh after Oct 11, 2026. Site placement: San Francisco's Census city point lies in the Pacific near the Farallon Islands, so the 103 UCSF rows that name the city without a usable ZIP (ZIP 94143; 102 trials) were drawn 50 road-miles from the city. City points now come from one table used both to assign a row to a county and to draw it: a point in no county's land takes the nearest county (23 coastal places), and a point more than a mile out to sea moves to where the county's residents 55+ live. A row whose registry state is wrong follows its ZIP when the stated city is a place of the ZIP's state at that ZIP, or other trials list the same facility there (19 rows: Mayo Clinic 'Rochester, New York, 55905' was in Monroe County, New York; Luminis 'Annapolis, Missouri' in Iron County; Gabrail 'Canton, Oklahoma' in Blaine County; Mary Crowley 'Dallas, Pennsylvania' in Luzerne County; Sibley Memorial, filed under Baltimore, is in the District of Columbia). A ZIP 25 or more miles from the stated city is a typing error when exactly one swap of two adjacent digits gives a ZIP inside that city (11 rows). New York and its boroughs map to their own counties; a city name that occurs twice in a state resolves to the largest place within 40 miles of the ZIP; a row with no usable ZIP follows the registry's other listings of the same facility in the same city (the Anschutz campus in Aurora, Colorado to Adams County; Dana-Farber to Suffolk County; Emory 30302 to DeKalb County). On the registry data of Oct 9, 2026 these placement rules move 138 rows and place 9 that had no county: counties with any trial 832 to 825 (Ashtabula, Ohio; Gage, Nebraska; Halifax, North Carolina; Skamania, Washington; Stewart, Tennessee; Iron, Missouri; Grimes, Texas and Blaine, Oklahoma lose a trial that is not there; Madison, Indiana gains its first); 380 limited and 82 broad menus unchanged; none within 60 road-miles 4.3% to 4.4% (4.293% to 4.375%: 80,988 more residents 55+ in 84 census tracts, each of whose only trial was a misplaced site; Oklahoma 12.5% to 15.2%, Nebraska 18.0% to 19.7%, Kentucky 1.6% to 2.2%, Tennessee 5.9% to 6.4%, Missouri 5.8% to 6.2%, Kansas 4.0% to 4.3%, North Carolina 1.0% to 1.2%, Texas 5.6% to 5.7%); fewer than 20 trials within 60 road-miles 12.0%, unchanged; Bay Area tracts gain up to 98 trials within 60 road-miles (a San Mateo County tract 338 to 417) without any share moving. Registry screen: non-muscle-invasive and muscle-invasive bladder cancer written as NMIBC/MIBC, mantle cell lymphoma written as MCL (but not the knee's MCL) and hemangioendothelioma count as cancer, and the registry search asks by name for light-chain (AL) amyloidosis, post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder and mantle cell lymphoma: 6 more trials on the same data (4,007 to 4,013; 27 site rows in 22 counties that each already have 65 to 1,052 trials, so no county crosses 1, 20 or 100 trials and no share moves). Science 37's virtual sites and 'at-home study' rows count as telemedicine (8 rows, none in the cancer data on Oct 9). Classifier: 36 trials change cancer type (29 their primary type): chronic myelomonocytic leukemia strings came out empty, so a CMML trial (NCT07033598) showed as Other / unclassified; myeloid sarcoma and histiocytic sarcomas are blood cancers, not Sarcoma; 'metastatic ... in the lung' and 'brain tumor - metastatic' no longer tag Lung or Brain; renal medullary carcinoma, sinonasal cancers, ETMR, ATRT, pineoblastoma, familial adenomatous polyposis, anal HSIL, misspelt 'hepatocellular' and HER2-expressing baskets are recognised. Other / unclassified 38 to 23 trials; the multi-cancer share 27.9% to 28.1%. No county's trial count and no access share moves from the screen or the classifier.

Not a change of method: the yearly sources were updated. Residents 55+ and household figures now come from the ACS 2020-2024 5-year release (was 2019-2023), and cancer incidence from State Cancer Profiles 2019-2023 (was 2018-2022), which, unlike the 2018-2022 release, includes Kansas counties. Measured on the same registry data (Oct 9, 2026) and the same rules: residents 55+ 98,596,429 to 100,019,672; fewer than 20 trials within 60 road-miles 12.0% (11.88 to 11.98 million people); none within 60 road-miles 4.4% to 4.3% (4.31 to 4.34 million); beyond 60 road-miles of a broad menu 38.1% to 38.0%; of an NCI center 43.7% (unchanged); no state moved more than half a point; no district's share beyond 60 road-miles moved a full point before rounding (AZ-9 and TX-36 show 1.0 after rounding), and in VA-9 the share living in a county with no trial site rose 80.2% to 84.0%. The new population split moved ZIP 24273 from Wise County to Norton city, Virginia, so two Ballad Health Norton site listings now count in Norton (0 to 2) instead of Wise (2 to 0). Counties with a published or small-numbers incidence rate 3,026 to 3,130 (Kansas); high-incidence, low-access counties 495 to 492.
